rows.speaker: Lan

rows.text: It's a turn-based game. You have to deal with me one time before you can go.
Your name is... Lan!
THEY ignore you and, in the blink of an eye, disappear from your sight.
rows.speaker: Lan

rows.text: "Don't be too discouraged. I will increase THEIR social attribute next time." Herta was a little disappointed, "THEY move too fast. But I was able to intercept some of THEIR information."
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: "THEY're probably not very familiar with Akivili." A moment passed. She added, "Perhaps THEY only have THEIR enemy, the Abundance, on THEIR mind."
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: The Hunt?
The Abundance?

"A tragic being, according to our record. They are bound by hatred and destiny, never to have even a moment's rest." You don't hear any hint of sympathy for said tragedy in her voice, "But that's life."
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: "Yeah, Yaoshi, the Aeon of Abundance," Herta answers indifferently. "The kindest being in the whole universe, probably also a monster. THEY would heal everything THEY see, be it as small as an atom or as large as a star system. Perhaps THEY can solve your Stellaron problem for you." She adds jokingly.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: "Look up." Herta says softly, "Someone worth getting excited about has appeared."
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: You look up and see a figure with six arms wantonly stretch THEIR body and bones, as if performing a cosmic dance.
rows.speaker: Yaoshi

rows.text: THEIR hair is like a magpie's feathers, blooming in a universe of thousands of stars, which reminds you of people's reverie about the Aeons recorded in the book. It's Yaoshi, the Aeon of Abundance.
rows.speaker: Yaoshi

rows.text: "The Trailblaze, I am delighted by your return." THEY stare at you with tens of thousands of eyes on THEIR body, with a voice so sympathetic, as if speaking to you in pity.
rows.speaker: Yaoshi

rows.text: You don't sound happy...
Don't keep staring at me, I'll blush.

"How can a body bounded by its limits cross the boundless oceans? May you give up your burdens, be removed from the cycle of being, and set yourself free from suffering." When THEY finish speaking, THEY kiss you and leave.
rows.speaker: Yaoshi

rows.text: You freeze in place, terrified. THEY stretch out THEIR poisonous scorpion-like hooked tail, and sting you lightly. You see wondrous scenes flashing before your eyes — vines grow wildly and entangle their beneficiaries, and there are abominations and crying everywhere.
rows.speaker: Yaoshi

rows.text: "Are you okay? Talk to me," said Herta with a dissatisfied voice, "well, that's fine. We will meet THEM again."
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: For some reason, you are suddenly sucked into darkness. This is a gravitational field where the curvature of space-time expands to its limit, and nothing – neither matter nor light – can escape.
rows.speaker: IX

rows.text: You feel yourself being swallowed by some black liquid — a sea of darkness. Your hearing and smell are cut off, and everything becomes far away from you.
rows.speaker: IX

rows.text: "Hey! What's going on..." You hear Herta's voice. "There's something wrong with your brainwaves. Hey..."
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: You stretch out your fingers, but still can't touch the vast, dark sea. You feel like a piece of grease floating on a dark sea of sorrow.
rows.speaker: IX

rows.text: "Cheer up, [Trailblazer]. I guess IX, the Aeon of Nihility, has appeared. THEY are nothingness, so the system cannot detect THEIR appearance." Herta says, "Your spirit is affected because IX is near you. You have meaning. You are an amazing person. You are loved and respected. You bring light and a future to our world. Now, keep playing the Simulated Universe. Quickly!"
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Herta's voice brings your distracted mind back.
rows.speaker: IX

rows.text: You only care about your Simulated Universe!
You don't care about me at all!
"Yeah, I forgot." She apologized emotionlessly, "Sorry for making you uncomfortable. Give me a sec. I'll collect some more data on IX, and then I'll get you out right away."
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: You hold your breath and try to stay focused. You seem to be able to hear toneless syllables deep in the void — it's THEIR voice.
rows.speaker: IX

rows.text: You look around and know that THEY are nearby, but cannot see THEIR presence. Maybe, THEY are right next to your ear... Soon, your spirit starts to break...
rows.speaker: IX

rows.text: "Stop, [Trailblazer]. You won't be able to hold it anymore." Herta says, "human minds will break when people get near IX, but IX doesn't seem to do it on purpose. Thank you for your hard work, you did a good job!"
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: The strange thing happened again. A chill creeps up your spine, mist clouds your eyes, and you see the familiar vision appearing again.
rows.speaker: Fuli

rows.text: This time, THEY are even closer – you can feel THEIR presence and power. Fuli, the Aeon of Remembrance, appears again. THEY float in midair, bowing THEIR head from above. Are THEY looking at you? But you are not sure which section is THEIR eyes.
rows.speaker: Fuli

rows.text: You tell yourself to stay sober and complete the mission: Speak to THEM.
rows.speaker: Fuli

rows.text: What a coincidence! We meet again.
How did you manage to control my mind?

"...chaos become time your dereliction determine past volume no longer proportional shrink steps one step two steps three feet depart prevent you be warned elio express advance baby fall cancer growing now..." THEY respond to you after hearing what you say. You feel the chill on your face, and the hairs on your skin shudder.
rows.speaker: Fuli

rows.text: Then THEY draw away and disappear in an instant. You feel relieved.
rows.speaker: Fuli

rows.text: You hear Herta's voice at just the right time. "You met Fuli again. Well done. Previous testers never even got a response from Fuli." Sounds like she has settled down from her excitement, and her voice has returned to the usual emotionless and mechanical register.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: You are still watching me?
Just what did you upgrade?

"Yup, sure am. Just treat it as the perk of being a rookie. Once you're familiar with the Simulated Universe, I won't bother you too much. There's so much to get done, so just play around by yourself."
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: "What do you think an upgrade is? The next version of a video game? Some tiny rewards handed out every one-and-half-months?" Herta snorts. "This is a whole micro-universe! If you could see all the changes at a glance, why would we spend all the time training a universe? I can just build a garden for your Express instead!"
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Herta sighs. "There's a Downloader just a little further ahead. Remember to use it to expand your team. Your brain is gradually adapting to the Simulated Universe, and the available RAM will gradually become accessible for you so you can play with more people. Alright, snap out of it. Go and choose your Blessing."
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: I suppose as the head of the Security Department, he should know.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Then let's go talk to him!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hey... you're all together?
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: Yep, we're from the Astral Express~
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Oh... Did Madam Herta send you to help?
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: It's just a coincidence. We came to deliver the rare relic Herta trusted us to find... We didn't expect to arrive during an invasion.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Why is the Antimatter Legion targeting you guys? It seems they just ignored the surface of the planet and came straight to the space station.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I... have no idea. The Legion came at a very suspicious time — almost right after the security system suddenly failed.
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: Lady... Lead Researcher Asta immediately began to organize the evacuation. I was supposed to cover everyone as they evacuated, but... I didn't expect to end up failing in this task.
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: Don't be too hard on yourself. Your leg and dominant hand were injured. It was a wise decision to hide here and avoid a head-on encounter with the Legion.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Yeah! Most of the staff have been evacuated safely, so right now our highest priority is to return to the master control zone and plan a counterattack! So... do you know how to use the elevator? I couldn't start it...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: An Aeon materializes nearby, and you recognize the familiar sensation. A vortex of energy approaches you and engulfs everything, annihilating every composite atom of your body in the collision. Burning rage and destructive desires tear you into a golden scar that is both your doom and a glimpse from Nanook the Destruction...
rows.speaker: Nanook

rows.text: The pain is over in an instant. You feel like a newborn.
rows.speaker: Simulated Universe

rows.text: "I'm sorry. This is my fault." You hear Herta's voice. "Nanook has never met Akivili. I didn't expect THEM to be so violent even towards an unknown Aeon. You were disintegrated instantly. I had to use system commands to restore a backup of you."
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: THEY're the Destruction, after all.
Please warn me next time.

"I know, I know. But if I tell you in advance, there's no way to collect reliable data." Herta says carelessly. "I'll ask Screwllum to protect you in advance. Next time you see the simulated Nanook, you'll give THEM a huge surprise — THEY won't be able to hurt you anymore. Well, that's it then. Great job. I'm gonna hang up."
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: You —

A dazzling white light captures your attention. You gaze up into the sky and see a comet streaking across. It is the brightest star you've ever seen, its brilliance as blinding as a dying star's. The comet disappears in a flash, leaving only a spot of residual light on your retina. There is the faint shadow of a person inside the light spot, but you can't really make it out.
rows.speaker: Lan

rows.text: "Lan of The Hunt..." Herta whispers. "THEY noticed you, but... THEY didn't stop for you." After a while, she adds, "Maybe THEY only care about THEIR nemesis, the Abundance."
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: The Hunt?
The Abundance?
"A tragic Aeon bound by hatred and destiny, never to have even a moment's rest." You don't hear any hint of sympathy for the said tragedy in her voice. "But that's life."
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: "Yeah, Yaoshi the Abundance," Herta answers indifferently. "The kindest being in the whole universe, probably also a monster. THEY would heal everything THEY see, be it as small as an atom or as large as a star system. Perhaps THEY can solve your Stellaron problem for you." She adds sardonically.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: A gentle sprinkling of light falls from the sky like a soft kiss. Yaoshi the Abundance steps out of thin air. With a smile on THEIR face and compassion knitted into THEIR brows, THEY seem unable to bear seeing you suffer in pain. As THEY walk, thorns sprout up and blossom in THEIR wake.
rows.speaker: Yaoshi

rows.text: "All sentient beings have three deaths — the death of the body, the death of thoughts, and the death of desires." The merciful Aeon whispers. "How can a body bounded by its limits cross the boundless oceans? The Trailblaze, may you give up your burdens, be removed from the cycle of being, and set yourself free from suffering." A thorn slowly floats towards you. Its flowers and leaves bloom before you, and its divine and enlightening nectar falls onto the tip of your tongue.
rows.speaker: Yaoshi

rows.text: Your pain and exhaustion have been swept away...
rows.speaker: Simulated Universe

rows.text: Yaoshi smiles and THEIR figure recedes into the distance.
rows.speaker: Yaoshi

rows.text: Suddenly, you feel sad. What's this about? Why are you even here? A gigantic machine of consciousness holds your mind hostage and transports you far away into the universe. Everything is false. Truth does not exist. Adventures are meaningless. Tragedy gloats like oil atop a sea of thought, quickly sinking into it to leave behind an enormous void...
rows.speaker: IX

rows.text: "Hey! What's going on — " A female voice is speaking. "There's something wrong with your brainwaves. Hey — "
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: That's unimportant. What are brain waves? Not important. You can live without knowing anything, just like a mindless baobab tree. You take in nutrients, grow, then die. Isn't that what life is? A moment of elation, after which there is nothing. Day after day, timeless and unchanging, having no future, having no light...
rows.speaker: IX

rows.text: "Ah, I get it."
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Yes, abandon all thoughts. Thoughts are burdens of action. Thoughts make you care and make you miserable. The leaves that drift with the current, the dust particles swirling in the wind, the boundless universe, and that black hole — black hole? You seem to realize something. A thought begins to struggle upward, like a drowning human violently beating against the waters. You fight through everything to gasp a breath. Very good. You're finally back. IX was influencing you.
rows.speaker: IX

rows.text: "Very good. You're finally back. IX was influencing you."
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: What happened?
IX?

"IX the Nihility appeared. THEY made you feel that everything is meaningless, and you almost became a vegetable in the Simulated Universe — Actually, it won't matter. I could've woken you up in reality. But you might not make it if this happens every time you meet IX." Herta sighs deeply. "This entity is truly nihilistic. THEY made THEMSELF so meaningless that the system didn't even detect THEM. I now believe that IX can destroy the whole universe with just a single thought."
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: "Cheer up, [Trailblazer]. IX's trick won't be so effective next time. You are important, really — Your life is very valuable, and there are many people who love you." She continues emotionlessly. "You have meaning. You are an amazing person. You are loved and respected. You bring light and a future to our world. Now, keep playing the Simulated Universe. Go!"
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: After the evacuation was complete, the elevators were all shut down to keep the Legion away from the master control zone.
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: Since Lady Asta sent you to look for me, I assume she must've given you the encryption key for accessing the elevator system?
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: Oh, right, she did give me some sort of card...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...March...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: But where did I put it...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You...
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: Ah! Here it is!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Let's go.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Hold on. I only activated the elevator on the highest floor. We'll have to go there to use it.
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: Why? It's so far away.
Okay.
Because I mustn't give the Legion any chance to reach the master control zone by the elevator. I must ensure the safety of the station's staff.
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: So I'll have to trouble you to take a bit of a detour... Apologies.
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: Sorry... This space station was entrusted to Lady Asta by Madam Herta. I must do this for the safety of the master control zone and the staff there.
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: So I'll have to trouble you to take a bit of a detour... Sincerest apologies.
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: Huh? You're not coming with us?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: My leg is injured... I'd only slow you down. I'll stay here and shut down the elevator once you've made it to the master control zone.
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: You won't slow us down. And you should be able to shut down the elevators from the master control zone, right?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Agreed. [Trailblazer] and I made it here safely, and now we've also got Dan Heng. We're more than enough to protect you~
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Let us worry about the Antimatter Legion. You just follow us and keep yourself alive~
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Trust us.
Don't overthink this.
You can use me as a crutch.
Aren't you a nice kid!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Thank you.
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: The repulsion bridge has been shut down?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Yes. To stall the enemy, more or less.
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: March, Dan Heng, you've been through a lot.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Whew, Himeko~ What took you so long! That last wave of Antimatter Legion came at us like a swarm of locusts, have you ever tried shooting locusts with a bow?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I wouldn't have made a difference. My orbital cannon can deal with a whole bunch of enemies at once, but I couldn't just blow up the space station with it — Herta would NOT like that...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Are you alright, Arlan? Asta's been worried about you.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I'm fine, a quick patching up will do. Thanks for asking. I'll report the situation to Lead Researcher Asta immediately. Bye.
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: Hey, nice to meet you. I'm Himeko, navigator of the Astral Express.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: In other words, she's in charge of where the Express goes.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: March hasn't been any trouble for you along the way, has she?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: [Trailblazer], think carefully about how you wanna reply to that.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...That's just my charm! And I didn't cause any trouble. You just have to get used to me... Look, Dan Heng agrees, right?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Oh, looks like we have two Dan Hengs on our team now.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Please leave me out of this.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Haha, look at you all, you've already gotten really close.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Come on, Asta has been worried about all of you.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Projectile radar tracking, normal. Telemetry signal frequency unusually high! Maintain at normal levels!
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Our measurements predict that the Legion is about to unleash over ten waves of continuous attacks. Everyone, brace yourselves!
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Asta! We're back!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Whew, I'm glad you're all back safe. Arlan just told me about the situation at the storage zone — and about his injury... thank you, for all your help.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: In times of disaster, I realize more and more that the space station's researchers are its most valuable assets... Alas, we were ill-prepared for such emergencies... we should have built up our security and combat departments.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: On the other hand, the entire crew of the Astral Express seems to be extraordinarily skilled.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: What is the current situation on the space station?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: The situation is under control for now. The damage to our security system was minor. The intruder only managed to alter a small amount of data, so it was easy to fix.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: The real problem lies with the researchers... They trust Madam Herta wholeheartedly and never thought that the space station would be breached by the Legion. A broken spirit is far worse than a broken body.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Let's go speak with the researchers. Right now, the space station can't afford any more unexpected turns, especially from within. Have you tried contacting Herta?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: [Trailblazer]? Nice to meet you. My name's Dan Heng, and this is March 7th.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: This space station was just attacked by the Antimatter Legion. We came to help with the rescue at the request of Lead Researcher Asta.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I sent multiple letters, all met with silence. You know her, Himeko, the space station is but a mere warehouse for followers and rare items. She doesn't really care about it.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: I knew it... No matter. I'll also send a letter to Herta and tell her that we've brought the rare item she seeks. At least that might get her attention.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: That would be of great help.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Hello, you must be... [Trailblazer], right? How can I help you?
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: This is Herta Space Station. As you might tell from its name, it belongs to the distinguished Madam Herta herself.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Herta Space Station was originally built as a warehouse for rare items and relics, but Madam Herta also allowed her followers to oversee tasks and conduct research. It then gradually turned into a scientific research base.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: The storage zone you passed through contains all our inventory, and is the main research center.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: The master control zone where we are now is the control center of the whole space station.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: It is said that the space station also contains Madam Herta's private chamber where her most precious, rare, and dangerous collections are sealed... And for someone like her, it's not out of the realm of possibility.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Even from me, the lead researcher, there are many things she keeps secret.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: I'm lead researcher of Herta Space Station. But honestly... I'm more like Madam Herta's "housekeeper" of this place.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Madam Herta is a genius, but managing disparate staff, tactfully representing the space station before the Intelligentsia Guild... these are all things beyond her abilities. But as it turns out they are my forte.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: I've never met a more reckless girl in my life.
I've never met a more lively girl in my life.
In that case, I'd rather not answer.
No matter how much they drone on about "Astronomy is just about looking at things, it doesn't bring any real value," they all fall silent in front of Madam Herta.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: No matter the problem, you just needed to say that it was Madam Herta's wishes and all would be fine. After all, Herta herself is a symbol of wisdom.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Hey, thanks to her, I can count the stars to sleep. Otherwise, I would've had to take over the family fortune. Just thinking about it terrifies me.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Arlan went to dress his wounds at the rest area. He knows himself well... but if he insists on pushing his limits, I'll give him a good earful.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: I'm very upset he didn't obey my orders and insisted on searching the storage zone even though everyone had already evacuated.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: I know he didn't want to leave any researchers behind... The Security Department is more than just a job to him.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: But Arlan doesn't care about getting hurt, he only cares about protecting others. It's the only way he feels... fulfilled.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: And it's not that I don't understand where he's coming from. I just want him to look out for himself, too!
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Herta... she's a member of the Genius Society. One of the proud favorites of the Aeon of Erudition. Ever since the birth of {RUBY_B#Aeon of Erudition}Nous{RUBY_E#}, there have only been 84 people admitted into the Genius Society.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: That is why Madam Herta is extremely... headstrong... She only pursues what interests her and as soon as that interest is lost, she abandons it and moves on. The space station was one such abandoned interest...
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: I have the right to remain silent.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Anyway, I lent out one of her manuscripts as a resource reference not long ago. It should still be in the master control zone. You can take a look if you wish.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Huh, chatting with you seems to have lightened my mood. It seems like talking can really raise one's spirits.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Well, that's the joy of youth! We should take every step forward full of energy! {M#He's}{F#She's} a discerning one, isn't {M#he}{F#she}, Dan Heng?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I have the right to remain silent.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: What's the matter, [Trailblazer]? You seem to have something on your mind.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Basically speaking, it's a train that travels through space. But more specifically, the Astral Express was a creation of the Aeon, Akivili the Trailblazer.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: As for what the Trailblaze, the Aeons, and Akivili are all about, let's talk about it when things have calmed down a little. I don't wanna overwhelm you now, do I?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Light Cones were created by the Garden of Recollection. These followers of the Aeon of {RUBY_B#Fuli}Remembrance{RUBY_E#} refined memory fragments to create Light Cones, which preserve memories.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: But you've already realized it, haven't you? Since Light Cones can preserve memories, they can also preserve experiences and abilities. That's why Light Cones are extremely precious rare items under level-2 restriction by the {RUBY_B#Galactic Monopoly}Interastral Peace Corporation{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: As far as I know, only the IPC possesses Light Cone technology authorized by the Garden of Recollection. I couldn't say what deal Herta made with the Garden, but knowing her, it was likely off the books...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You should cherish every Light Cone. They are all precious memories of their original owners.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Who exactly you are escapes me, but you seem familiar to me.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I have a couple of hunches, but I can't prove any at this point. So, they'll be my little secrets for now.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Are you concerned about your past? You seem like someone who prefers to look forward rather than back... Or maybe I'm just describing myself.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Come to me anytime if you have more questions.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I'll leave the reassurance of the researchers in your hands.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: If you have any other questions, you are welcome to come to Himeko and me.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: ...If only I'd caught the Antimatter Legion sooner...
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: Push the stick down, Alfred... Sorry, sorry, I got the wrong person.
rows.speaker: Hinkel

rows.text: Let me help.
How're you feeling?
How's the space station?
What's Asta like?
Alright, I'll leave you to get some rest.
I'm fine, this pain is nothing, really. I'm used to it. In fact, I should be proud of it. It's a reminder of being able to protect everyone.
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: Ahem, but don't tell Lead Researcher Asta what I just said.
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: There were a few researchers who didn't make it...
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: The rest are fine, mostly minor injuries. But I'm worried about their mental states.
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: Most of them came to the space station because they admired Madam Herta. But now they can't reach her or even their own families. I just hope they can all survive this crisis.
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: My first impression was that she was the daughter of a rich family — owners of a big company.
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: She was kind to me though. When she went to the space station, I followed her.
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: I don't know much about science, but I'm glad to be able to protect people in pursuit of their research.
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: I hope all this chaos will end soon.
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: Thanks, kid. We're doing some pre-checks for the satellite remote sensing. I'll hold down the button to monitor the signal, and you push the control stick according to my instructions.
rows.speaker: Hinkel

rows.text: But first let's talk about the controls. "Up" is the spectrometer, "Down" is the filter, "Left" is the reference level, and "Right" is the attenuator.
rows.speaker: Hinkel

rows.text: Our pre-checks have three steps. Turning on the spectrometer, then the attenuator, and finally outputting the signal to the filter.
rows.speaker: Hinkel

rows.speaker: Eikura Shuu

I'd like to learn about the space station.
I'd like to learn about you.
I'd like to learn about Arlan.
I'd like to learn about Herta.
I don't have any more questions.
It's dangerous outside.
Don't be a hero.
Injured? I don't care, see anyone else that cares? Who are you anyway, get out of my way.
rows.speaker: Eikura Shuu

rows.text: Dangerous? Of course it's dangerous, I just came back from the front line, I know that better than you.
rows.speaker: Eikura Shuu

rows.text: Hero? Don't overthink it. I'm not doing this for others, I'm doing it for myself.
rows.speaker: Eikura Shuu

rows.text: The space station shield's first line of defense is the anti-gravity ionizing grid. I'm the researcher in charge of it. Do you expect me to just sit here after something like this?
rows.speaker: Eikura Shuu

rows.text: It's not your fault.
It's over now.
Hehe, scholars are a lot easier to deal with than those vociferous old geezers back at home.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Please, just stay here.
I agree. But when the investigation's over, the blame will fall entirely on my shoulders.
rows.speaker: Eikura Shuu

rows.text: That may be the case, but it's better than just hiding here doing nothing.
rows.speaker: Eikura Shuu

rows.text: Hmph... it's easy for you to say! This didn't happen on your watch, you wouldn't understand!
rows.speaker: Eikura Shuu

rows.text: Lesley! Sir, I need to go. I need to go find Lesley.
rows.speaker: Rocky

rows.text: Stupid boy, is your head not screwed on right? You're leaving over my dead body.
rows.speaker: Bernard

rows.text: I'll knock some sense into you yet... Hey, where do you think you're go— Argh...
rows.speaker: Bernard

rows.speaker: Emily

rows.text: ...That's bitter coffee... *coughing* ...so bitter.
rows.speaker: Emily

rows.text: Too dang bitter!!!
rows.speaker: Emily

rows.text: Oh sis, where are you? I'm so scared...
rows.speaker: Emily

rows.speaker: Lukacs

rows.text: I'd like to learn about the Astral Express.
I'd like to learn about Light Cones.
Do you... know who I am?
I don't have any more questions.
They may be part of the rare item collection, but are they not also living things? Don't their rights deserve to be protected!?
rows.speaker: Lukacs

rows.text: Non-human life?
Rare item collection?
Protecting their rights?
Yes. Non. Human. Life. Living creatures that aren't human...
rows.speaker: Lukacs

rows.text: ...Some of which have been collected as rare items and housed in the space station. Most of the researchers disregard their basic rights.
rows.speaker: Lukacs

rows.text: Even now, with death staring them in the face, they still refuse to open their minds.
rows.speaker: Lukacs

rows.text: And I, Lukacs, outstanding researcher of the Herta Department of Galactic Geopolitics, must awaken those pretending to sleep!
rows.speaker: Lukacs

rows.text: At the space station, we've always collected rare items — countless articles from across the galaxy. But not everyone knows that among these articles are also living things.
rows.speaker: Lukacs

rows.text: And I, Lukacs, outstanding researcher of the Herta Department of Galactic Geopolitics, must emphasize in this time of crisis that their lives and rights should also be respected!
rows.speaker: Lukacs

rows.text: Exactly! And I, Lukacs, outstanding researcher of the Herta Department of Galactic Geopolitics, shall continue fighting and speaking up for the rights of all non-human life in these terrible times!
rows.speaker: Lukacs

rows.text: If you are interested in joining the cause, please stand by my side and repeat after me!
rows.speaker: Lukacs

rows.text: All together! Protect rare item rights...!
rows.speaker: Lukacs

Save non-human life!
I think I should leave.
You did well, friend! Follow my rhythm, and say it loud, with conviction!
rows.speaker: Lukacs

rows.speaker: Lukacs

rows.speaker: Lukacs

rows.speaker: Gunn

rows.text: Home planet? My home planet? ...I do not understand what you are saying.
rows.speaker: Sheila

rows.text: Never mind. If Sheila could hear this, she'd understand.

rows.speaker: Mare

rows.speaker: Adler

rows.speaker: Lukacs

rows.text: Waaaah!

rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Protect rare item rights! Save non-human life!
rows.speaker: Lukacs

rows.text: [Trailblazer]?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...As you say so. Alright, what should we do next?

Alright, give the poor child a break, Herta.

rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: How were THEY created? Why were THEY created? What were THEY created for? [Trailblazer], have you ever thought about these questions?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Well indeed, it's got nothing to do with you, but we need you. Give me some time, [Trailblazer], I'll make this worthwhile for you too.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: 42 what? Are you even listening to me? We want to solve the mystery behind the Aeons! Right now I want you to participate in this project!
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Oh really? That's what my partners said as well. Fine, I am a team player. Then let's call it the "Simulated Universe."
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Not bad. It would've been even better if you didn't faint. But thanks to you, the Doomsday Beast was as tame as a kitten. It had no temper at all.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Did we win?
Even the Doomsday Beast, is no match...
Who am I, where am I...
Yes, and you are the hero.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Get up when you feel better. Himeko wants you to go find her. I have something to do, so I won't go with you, alright?

rows.text: By the way, we should exchange beacons. If you get lost or something, feel free to text me.

rows.speaker: Herta

rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Er, you are kidding, right...?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It's good that you've made it through in one piece. You can rest easy now that the threat from the Legion has been neutralized.

rows.text: I guess I'll leave you to rest up a bit for the time being. By the way, what's your beacon address? That way if anything happens, I can contact you.

Hmm, truly amazing! I built a whole space station just to contain this unactivated Stellaron and keep The Blue from disaster...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: You're not wrong, but be careful about blurting things out loud — it could attract unwanted attention.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Well, this is the Herta Space Station.

rows.text: You're right. This little one's body truly is strange...

My name is [Trailblazer].

Hah! Compared to me, you are. How old are you even?

rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: That's... beside the point. Hey is this one the same kind as that March 7th? If that were true...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Alright, [Trailblazer]. I got it. But I'm still gonna call you little twerp. The space in my brain is too valuable to store peoples' names.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Oh! Well, thanks for remembering my name then.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: That's different. We have business with each other. Umm, what was your name again?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Forget it, let's focus on the one who can store a Stellaron in their body...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: You can leave. I'm discussing science with what's her face... Himeko? Science exists in objectivity, there's nothing to be secretive about.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: But as far as you're concerned, I think it would be better for you to listen in. After all, I have a lot of plans ahead involving you. Speaking of which, Himeko...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Oh, it's you, [Trailblazer]... Do you have something on your mind?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Can I bring {M#him}{F#her} in for some research?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Oh? What did I do?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: You're always the first one to charge into battle.
Your judgments are always accurate.
Is that so? Well, I am the train's guard. I suppose it's just instinct.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: It's about being observant at all times and carefully making the best choice for the situation. You can do it too.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I think you're not bad yourself, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: If you're referring to what I think about you joining the Astral Express... You're overthinking it.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: My position is simple: It doesn't matter to me. I suggest you ignore my opinions and make your own choice.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Being on the Express isn't exactly the same as "traveling" or "adventuring..." The Astral Express symbolizes "trailblazing" you understand?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Trailblazing implies the unknown, be it unknown risks or unknown rewards.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: In my opinion, the unknown is no more terrifying than the known... In fact, the unknown signifies something we can control and change.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I'm a little hesitant.
I understand.
Don't use hesitation as an excuse. If you hesitate for too long, your original way of thinking will eventually cease to exist.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Mm, okay then.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Hey, [Trailblazer]! I heard the news. You're coming with us on the Express, right?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I haven't decided yet!
Do you want me to come along?
Oh come on, you know that's what you want deep down inside. I can see it on your face.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Do I even need to say it? I think we're becoming fast friends... isn't that enough?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: But you look like you've got something on your mind... come on, out with it!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Getting nostalgic already?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Y'know, when you were passed out, all I thought was I had to look after you. And then you picked up the bat! Just incredible!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: In the blink of an eye, you knocked that big fella into Mr. Yang's black hole and saved me... I still haven't thanked you properly yet...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Nah, we're not splitting up here...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I'd like to know too, because I was already on the Express when I woke up.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I was just drifting out there in space and got picked up by the Express. Amazing, right?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Crazy stuff like that? Not too often. It sure freaked me out.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: But every encounter I've had since coming aboard the Express has been strange to say the least.
rows.speaker: March 7th
