rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Huh... looking back now, it all seems quite dangerous... But I had the crew there with me, so the problems didn't seem all that bad.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Of course you should! Why wouldn't you?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: There's only four of us now, plus Pom-Pom. Each of us can have our own carriage to sleep in! You wouldn't have the heart to leave your carriage unmanned, would you?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: How did you get here so soon?
Sorry if I kept you waiting.
That sounds more like a problem for you guys.
I don't know what the carriage is like.
Join us, [Trailblazer]. Then it wouldn't be a problem anymore.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Then come aboard and take a look for yourself.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: All the time.
What's this got to do with me?
Still haven't made up your mind? Fine. Since I'm interested in you, I'll answer any questions you have.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Me? Hmm, well, Talking about oneself is as pointless as it gets.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Stellarons, huh? Ask away, I'm listening.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: I call it the "Metaverse"!
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Seriously? Don't ride that hype train.
Let's just keep it simple.
The Express? Shouldn't you be asking Himeko instead?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: [Trailblazer], thank goodness you're all safe.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: It's a pity that we haven't had the chance to talk much, and now the Express is about to leave. Do you have any questions?
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Madam Herta gave me a piece of code, which she apparently wrote on the way here. I just tried it out and the defense shield's regenerating three times faster than before.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Space station... Herta...?
You're... a robot?
Heh, Genius Society...
Thanks to her, the Antimatter Legion outside is not much of a threat anymore. The space station's repairs and reconstruction can also begin smoothly, but internally...
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: When the Stellaron was extracted, even for that brief moment, it corroded the space station and formed a new space — what we now call the Fragmentum.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Hello there~
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hi.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: The part that was corroded is irreversible, so the space station will always be in a state of quasi-Fragmentum.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: There are strange bubbles at the space station...
About Stellarons...
About the Express...
About the decision...
Let me think things over.
About Herta...
Oh, this is a top secret. Outsiders can never know that I own this thing. You must sign a non-disclosure agreement first.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: What's inside?
Fine. I'll sign it.
I'll consider it.
I won't tell you a thing before you sign the agreement.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Great...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: What are the effects of the Fragmentum?
Suit yourself.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Will I also be corroded by the Fragmentum?

You take the paper and pen from Herta and leave your signature. The paper is made from a bizarre material, and the ink dries up the moment it touches the paper. When you move the tip of the pen away, your heart suddenly flutters.

Please bear in mind that this agreement is more than a legally binding contract. You must also abide by the law of the Imaginary, which is above the social and natural laws. Not even the IPC can override it.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Why didn't you say that before I signed the agreement?
Law of the Imaginary?
Can I sign another agreement to nullify this non-disclosure agreement?
All existing Fragmentums are connected, so there will be monsters that will enter the space station through its Fragmentum.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Would you have refused to sign if I'd told you that? You seem like the kind who doesn't think much about consequences. You will make a decision regardless of its price.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Uh, what decision? You're gonna have to be more specific.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: It is the law of the universe and the world — the only unbreakable law.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: You're the master of the space station?
You really are a terrible person.
What do you actually look like?
I still have some questions...
Don't worry. If I want to swindle you, you'll never see it coming.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: On paper, yes. But I don't really care about this place. I built it, put some stuff in, left some people here, and let them just manage themselves.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Asta's the lead researcher of the space station, so for all intents and purposes, she's the master. I reject the concept of ownership because I don't want the responsibilities that come with it.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Now that you have signed the agreement, you can do anything you like with my Memory Bubbles. Just make sure you are out of the sight of entities from the Garden of Recollection. In fact, I don't think there will be any trouble even if they catch you...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: It doesn't matter. Who cares if others don't like me? I know I don't care. As long as I have my own value, I can do whatever I want.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: While you may have good character, do you have any value? Don't take that the wrong way, I'm genuinely asking you. You might have some value, I just don't know about it.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Memory Bubble?
The Garden of Recollection?
Who are the Memokeepers?
Can I touch the bubble now?
Human, female, young, beautiful, attractive.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Not much different from what you're seeing now. I modeled it after how I looked, back when I was a kid. It might not be identical, but I'd say maybe 70, 80 percent there?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Oh, I was so precocious — all I cared about back then was solving the solitary wave problem, ignoring my precious childhood...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: The Garden of Recollection has ways to steal the memories of others. To preserve memories, they created a Sentiention membrane to keep the memories wrapped up in it like a bubble, making it easy to carry memories around.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: They have an even more advanced technology called Light Cones. With that, they can capture more than just memories... It's a shame that I can never master the Light Cone technology without the Blessing of the Aeon Fuli.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: It is a faction that worships the Aeon Fuli. In their opinion, the world is defined by everyone's perception, and memories are the proof of the world's existence. They are willing to forgo their physical bodies for that purpose.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: If you ask me, the Garden of Recollection, the Architects, The Family, and the Antimatter Legion are all idiots. They obsessively worship their Aeons.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: What exactly is a Stellaron?
Do you know about the Stellaron Hunters?
Why am I able to host the Stellaron?

They are members of the Garden of Recollection who travel between worlds to collect precious memories. You will run into them sooner or later. I bet the memory of a Astral Express passenger is highly sought after by them.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: You could get lucky if you meet civilized Memokeepers, since they might use an amazing memory to exchange with yours. However, watch out for the Memosnatchers, the radicals in the Garden of Recollection. They won't give you a heads-up before stealing your memory.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: According to my research, it's a type of lifeform with a special property that tethers it to a certain Path or Aeon's power.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Wherever it's located, it responds to that world's desires to advance its civilization. But, this comes at the cost of some form of disaster. The mechanism behind it is likely related to Nanook the Destruction.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Sure~ Just touch it with your forehead. Remember to close your eyes, or your head will start spinning.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Oh, that weird bunch. I'm satisfied with just one Stellaron, but they've scoured the universe, obtained several, and still aren't satisfied. I don't know what their true intentions are.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Genius Society #76}Screwllum{RUBY_E#} went up against the Stellaron Hunters before. I heard there was a member whose hacking skills were on par with Screwllum.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Being on the same level as Screwllum — who's probably the best in the universe — is nothing short of spectacular. It's beyond my abilities, computers are not my forte.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Ha... That I don't know. Which is why I'm gearing up to solve this mystery.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: What's the Astral Express like?
Do you trust the Astral Express?
What's your relationship with them?
You mean how it looks? Like a train. Well...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: I was very interested in the Express for a while, and wrote a lot of papers, but forgot where I left them. Now I can't remember anything about it.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Uh-huh.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: We've been business partners for a long time.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Every once in a while, I'll need them to get me things from other planets, and they often come to me to help them solve problems.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Can I return to the space station?
So I should board the Express?
Do I have any other choice?
Can I stay at the space station?
I really want to stay.
Can I stay at the space station?
Of course, I'll still be here waiting for you, eh... and the space station will be waiting for you. Returning... it's not impossible.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: If you wanna be a researcher here, you can just ask Asta. If she's fine with it, I have no complaints.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: No, hold on — you have a Stellaron within you. I think it's better if you left and came back occasionally. It might be dangerous if you stay for too long...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: No. You're way too dangerous. I don't mind personally, but I don't want Asta and others to take the risk.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: You wouldn't want the Stellaron in you to hurt all the people in the space station either, right?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Just come back once in a while. You will always be welcome at the space station — just don't stay for too long.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: ...You really are weird. What's so good about this place? Even I don't like staying here...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Ugh. Fine. To be honest with you, I have plenty of ways to seal a mere Stellaron — You just might end up not having a lot of personal freedom.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: If you're so keen to stay... Fine. I'm okay with it. Go speak to Asta. She's the lead researcher. She's in charge.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: As I've said, talk to Asta! She's the lead researcher. She's in charge. Go, go, go.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Well, from an objective standpoint, that's the most rational place for you to be.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: First of all, you have somewhere to live. And you'd be under their protection. Also, it'll be a long trip, so you'll have more opportunities to find a way to save yourself from the Stellaron. Lastly, if the Stellaron really explodes, you won't harm too many people around you.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Oh, how should I know! It's up to you, you have so many options to choose from. Maybe jump out a hatch, or hop into the Fragmentum and see if any monsters start worshiping you?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Okay, suit yourself.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Ahh, I'd like to know the answer to that as well.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: All existing Fragmentums are connected, so monsters will be able to enter the space station through the Fragmentum here. But it shouldn't allow anything to exit your body, so...
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Is the damage to the space station serious?
Make sure you don't burn yourself out.
I talked with Arlan and there's no easy solution to this problem at the moment. We can only increase the security and patrol frequency to protect the ongoing research.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Is there really no way I can help?
Let me think things over.
Can I stay at the space station?
After all this is over, I'm putting my vacation time in with Madam Herta. I've got it all planned. I'll hop on an airship and give The Blue a good look.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: You can see it from the space station, you know?
Will Madam Herta let you take a vacation?
Be that as it may, taking it in while on vacation and observing it during work are not the same thing.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: I guess so? I haven't taken leave once since I joined the space station...
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: And if I have an actual, full vacation, I can take my time to collect observational data and finish writing my paper.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Of course, there's already a lot of published research on The Blue, but I want to study it myself. It might sound a lot like work, but it's really just a hobby — there are no deadlines or quotas to meet, and I don't get paid.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: I like you, but... you have a Stellaron in your body.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: If you were just wandering around, or if you agreed to be sealed away in an experiment pod, that would be fine.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: But if you're going to work in the space station long-term, the Stellaron may have some serious effects on the station's Fragmentum. As the lead researcher, that's a risk I cannot take.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: I can sense your enthusiasm for the space station, but I'm afraid I have to turn you away.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Herta says I can stay.
Huh? Madam Herta said that?
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: In that case... I have nothing against it either. Mind you, if Madam Herta was to do something to you, [Trailblazer]...
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: She's not going to care a lot about what you think.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: If you wanted to come back and help, of course, I wouldn't refuse you. Dan Heng helped inventory our rare items, March 7th said that she would help out as much as she can and connected over 50 wires in the electrical room. Everyone from the Express is so obliging...
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: And I think you're pretty good at "meddling" too, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Sure, no hurry.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: What do you think? Does the Astral Express look the same as you imagined?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: As I expected, it looks like a train.
I feel like it's missing something...
Everyone on the Express is a passenger.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: We're all heading towards an unknown destination, like we are traveling together.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Maybe that's why the Trailblaze chose such a look.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: March said something like that at first, too.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Seems like you young people have similar tastes.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Oh right — March and Dan Heng should both be in their rooms right now.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You can go look for them. You youngsters should get along well.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Are their rooms fun?
What about here...?
Ah, you know, young people! Their rooms always reflect their personality.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You can go and... have a look around?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: We usually meet up here, but our personal cabins are in the next carriage.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Oh how time flies.
How did you join the Express?
Does that kind of thing happen often?
I'm thinking about if I should get on the Express...
Let me think things over.
Also, don't mind Pom-Pom's antics. They're actually pretty interested in you. It's just that we haven't had new passengers on the Express for a long while.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I won't steal Pom-Pom's thunder. If you have any questions, just go ask our conductor.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Himeko likes using the Phonograph a lot. She says it can play melodies from the past.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Welt likes collecting these jet-black discs. It seems like they could be antiques. He'd be very happy if you could bring a few back.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Here already? I was just engaging in pleasantries. How can I help?
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Hey! Y—You don't have any questions to ask Pom-Pom!?
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Is it because you think Pom-Pom talks too much? Or is it Pom-Pom's age? You youngsters gotta learn to bridge that generation gap.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Where's March 7th's room?
About Dan Heng's room...
Is that a... phonograph?
Oh? Why are you interested in her room?
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Ah, Pom-Pom remembers Himeko saying that you saved her...
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Mmm, very brave! Very foolhardy! But that is what a Trailblazer should be like.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: March 7th's room is in the Express Sleeper Compartment. She's always running around, so she might not be there.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Dan Heng's room? Oh, you mean the archives.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: He's just... sort of living in there, I guess. I can't be bothered getting him out.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: I'll be waiting for you, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: March 7th's room is right next to the Archives. You can visit him on the way.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: You're really good at taking care of others.
I didn't think you approved of me.
You don't seem like someone who likes to travel.
Let me think things over.
You recognize this as well?
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Himeko always likes to bring back weird junk and try to fix it.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: That also got modified a bit.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: That's all my questions for today.
Pom-Pom still needs to prepare for the Express' warp jump. You can look around the place yourself.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: No matter where you go on this train, Pom-Pom will always have my eyes on you.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: You just left. Why are you back again!?
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Go, go. I'm busy here and I don't have time for you.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: (There seems to be the sound of electronic equipment...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Hm? Who's there?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: It's me, [Trailblazer].
I haven't even knocked...
...Oh, it's you. The door's not locked. Come in.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I learned to sense incoming visitors after people kept barging in so frequently.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Can I help you?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Dan Heng gives a slight nod and shifts his gaze elsewhere.
Just looking around.
Feel free. This is open to everyone on the Express.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: While many of the roads that Akivili traveled along no longer exist, I think it's still meaningful to record our adventures as current passengers of the Express.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I enter the collected data into the archives' data bank. I try to catalog the people and places the Express encounters, and compare and contrast them with the existing records.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Do you see the terminal over there? It can be used to view information already stored in the data bank. Do give it a go.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Is that a... phonograph?
You recognize this as well?
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: (But... can he really sleep on such a hard bed?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: A hard bed is good for your spine. A bed that's too soft will end up hurting you.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: There's a vending machine too?
Shouldn't be a surprise to see the IPC's vending machine anywhere...
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: This thing might add some nice flavor to the trip.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: That's all my questions for today.
(How did he know... Did my gaze betray me!?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I'll be entering any new information we encounter on future journeys, so drop by anytime to check it out. We also have a shortcut on the terminal device.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I didn't take you to be a scholar.
I didn't know you could fix computers so well.
Seems like you have some deep misunderstandings about me. *sigh* Ah, well, I think I know who caused that.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Y'know, I'm not... *sigh*
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I have matters to attend to, feel free.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: So, if you're headed next door...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...keep it down.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: (The door is unlocked. Should I go in?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (You knock, but there's no response...)
(Just one look should be fine, right?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Just a little peek?
Never mind.
Make a choice I won't regret... reach the future...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (So much has happened in such a short time...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (Better to wait till the room's owner comes back.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I came to visit your pad.
This is not my pad, it's just where I sleep.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: These are the Archives. It has the records of all the Astral Express's trips since its first journey.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: A lot of the data is corrupted, but even the residual pieces contain huge amounts of information that we're struggling to process. I'm trying to sort them out.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Are you sorting out the data?
Any fun ones?
Yes, just my personal interest.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Aside from the existing data, I also recorded this trip to the archives.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Ahem, hi, hello~ Attention all passengers. Attention all passengers.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: The Express is about to conduct a warp jump. All passengers, please gather at the main hall.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: I repeat. The Express is about to conduct a warp jump. All passengers, please gather at the main hall.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Go look them up yourself. I don't know your definition of "fun."
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: If you see your own name, don't be surprised, I also recorded this trip to the archives.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: (Did March 7th take all these pictures...?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (There are even pictures of the space station...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: You took long enough! But at least everyone's here now.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Where is Dan Heng?
He won't be here, so just leave him be.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Oh yeah, take these.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: What's this?
Just a little gift from the conductor to the passenger. Think of it as an investment in your future growth.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Okay everyone, hurry up and find a place to sit down. Try not to be like March, always running around the Express like a headless chicken.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Pom-Pom's going to start the final preparations for the jump.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: What's wrong? You look like you were about to say something.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Oh, I think I know what you were going to ask. You've come to the right person.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Ohh, you want to know more about the Express? I'm glad. After all, it's an important companion of ours.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The cosmos is endlessly vast. Asking me that all of a sudden... I'm not even sure where to begin.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: "Trailblaze" is our mission and the source of strength that powers the Express to travel across the galaxy.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Pom-Pom doesn't wanna admit it, but they really do have everything you may need on sale.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: This is your first time experiencing the warp jump, so a little discomfort is unavoidable.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: If you're really anxious about it, I can stay here and have a chat with you.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: About everyone on the Express? Who would you like to know about?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: It's impossible to trace the origin of this phenomenon. When it's observed by humans — or I should say once it begins to affect the physical world — it's already too late to reverse.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: It's like a sudden storm that appears on a calm ocean. This phenomenon causes the smooth journey through the expanse to be filled with dangers.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: The mechanism whereby this mutation and corrosion spreads is the Stellarons.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: It promulgated rapidly like cancer cells, so the Interastral Peace Corporation named it the Cancer of All Worlds.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: They are an army ruled by the Aeon of Destruction, Nanook.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: As Nanook's followers, they stand against all life and civilization and execute the will of Destruction, disseminating chaos and calamity.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Their actions cannot be explained by reason, because their only motivation and purpose is to destroy.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: There is only one thin quilt, but it looks very warm. Being surrounded by all the books and records provides a surprising sense of security.
The Fragmentums are a phenomenon of corrosion.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: The mainstream school of thought is that Stellarons catalyzed the appearance of Fragmentums.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: All matter and space that comes into contact with the Fragmentum will be turned into Fragmentum creations.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: However, you don't have to feel too burdened. At the very least, the current state of the Stellaron in your body is very stable and will not cause distortion to the outside.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: There you are!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Wait, this is your first trip! So that should be double the excitement, right?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The first step is to grab a hold of the root cause of your anxiety.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You can't just grab something like that!
OK, I got it.
Well, it is a little abstract, but basically you just need to pinpoint what's bothering you.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You really got it, huh!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I'm ready, I'm ready to go!
But... I'm still a little worried about what lies ahead.
The second step is to focus all your anxiety on that point.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Is this some sort of mumbo jumbo about transferring consciousness?
Okay, I'm ready for step three.
This is science! Don't get distracted! *deep breath* Focus.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Seems like you're a natural. It's not easy to reach this level of enlightenment.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Now for step three: Yank out that anxiety and cast it away with all your might!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Come on, that's just using psychological suggestion!
Okay, well I've cast out all the anxiety now.
That doesn't mean it won't work! The best method for relieving anxiety is the one that works, right?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Really? I've never been able to do it successfully myself!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: What does it feel like? Like all your worries have been swept away?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: [Trailblazer], can you see this message? If you do, just {LAYOUT_MOBILE#tap}{LAYOUT_CONTROLLER#press}{LAYOUT_KEYBOARD#click} anywhere on the screen —
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: See? You can move around now. I want you to play Akivili and find some monsters to fight. Let's see which simulated Aeon will notice you first.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: There is a murmur in the amber sky. It's dusk. You look up and find countless copper ore, amber and opal falling from the sky. This is a wondrous mineral rain. In the steam, the colossal thing stretched THEIR spine from the mantle with a sledgehammer gripped in THEIR broad palm. You opened your eyes and realized that this is actually Qlipoth, the Aeon of Preservation!
rows.speaker: Qlipoth

rows.text: Is this a new trick by Herta?
Is this some kind of role-playing?
Ah! You're just like Mr. Yang, always worrying about things that haven't even happened yet.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Young people should be energetic! Here, let's do some relaxation exercises.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That's the spirit!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hehe, I was excited the first time I experienced a warp jump, too. But I'm used to it now.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Don't worry, you'll get used to it too, and before you know it you'll be a mature and dependable passenger just like me.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: There is a huge roar around THEM – this is a warning for you. Then, THEY disappear before your eyes.
rows.speaker: Qlipoth

rows.text: "Our calculations are correct. Qlipoth, the Aeon of Preservation, has really appeared." Herta's voice suddenly sounded, and she let out an ambiguous giggle, "The Aeon of Trailblaze, Akivili's revival has attracted an old friend."
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: About the Express...
About the galaxy...
About Trailblaze...
I don't have any more questions.
But THEY have run away.
About the history of the Express...
About where the Express is headed...
About the Express' source of power...
About Akivili...
I have another question...

The Astral Express was a tool created by Akivili the Trailblaze, who used it to transport THEMSELF and the Nameless across the galaxy. It is rumored that there are other vehicles like it, but the Express has no such records.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: When I found the Express, its memory had been severely damaged, with much of its valuable information lost. All I know is that the Express is an Aspect of Creation built by Akivili themself, and used to travel the cosmos.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: As for how it was built and how it was damaged, I do not have an answer.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The Express is traveling on a route that the Trailblaze once embarked on. The names of some destinations have been lost, but the first and final stops were both at Pegana — Akivili's home world.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: We speculate the Astral Express started its journey from Pegana, stopping at each destination along the way before returning there for its next journey. However, the appearance of the Stellarons has caused a delay at each stop.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: There is a legend in the galaxy: The heart of Akivili themself lies in the core of the Astral Express, providing it with the power to travel between worlds. But I found no evidence of that aboard the Express.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Besides, the Express existed before the Trailblaze fell. There's no way they could have had two hearts, right? However, it is likely that the Express possesses some sort of mechanism to transfer power from the Trailblaze.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: It wouldn't be possible with a normal Pathstrider.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The fallen Aeon, deceased Trailblaze — THEIR passing is still a mystery, but of all the known Aeons, Akivili was the closest to mankind.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: In the databank aboard the Express, it is recorded that THEY walked among the mortals — adventuring, fighting, and celebrating with THEM. Although THEY were an Aeon restrained by the "Primum Mobile," Akivili enjoyed a freedom similar to us mortals.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: THEY were different from most... But THEIR passing came so suddenly that it was thought THEY were killed by another Aeon. I don't believe that to be the case.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Tell me more stories about the relationship between the Aeons!
About its nature...
About the Aeons...
About the factions...
About the Paths...
I have another question...
I've been to many different worlds, yet I still know very little about the galaxy, simply because it's too vast. As for its nature, there are a few theories that I can share with you.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The most popular is probably the Cosmos Tree theory, proposed by Zandar, Emanator of Erudition and the first member of the Genius Society. He compared the cosmos to an enormous imaginary tree, with its leaves being individual galaxies.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Therefore, only Aeons, who draw their energy from the imaginary, and Emanators, who are blessed by Aeons, can travel through the spaces filled with imaginary energy. That's why planets where civilizations exist are so similar.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: However, the theory has its flaws. Elias Salas, the 56th member of the Genius Society, invented remote detection, disproving that the imaginary is unique. This shook the foundation of the "Cosmos Tree" theory.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: There are other theories as well: The "Stretching" theory, the "Heat Torch" theory, and the "Parallel Imaging" theory... The Riddlers claim the galaxy is just a dream and IX's followers seem to like that claim.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Aeons are the most mysterious beings in the galaxy. All we know is that THEY ascended from the form of intelligent beings. As for the how and why, even the geniuses over at the Genius Society haven't the slightest clue.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Upon ascending to Aeon-hood, that being gains power over the Paths, free to choose the allocation of imaginary energy however THEY wish, while suffering the restrictions of the "Primum Mobile."
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The Aeon of Destruction seeks only to destroy the universe, while the Aeon of Erudition wants to find the answer for all that exists. Meanwhile, the Aeon of Preservation continues to forge walls, and the Aeon of Enigmata devotes themself to obscuring all that is known...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: A cloud of mystery shrouds the Aeons. I heard Madam Herta recruited a team to try and solve the mysteries about THEM.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Compared to the Aeons, the factions are much easier to understand. Mortals with the same objective gather together to practice their understanding of Aeons and the Paths.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Many Aeons are unreachable, but the factions are close to us. After Akivili trailblazed across the galaxy, people became aware of the existence of other worlds. Gradually, more people started trying to use the power of the Aeons to travel between worlds.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The Interastral Peace Corporation is a good example: They worship Qlipoth, the Aeon of Preservation, but somehow became the largest economic entity in the galaxy;
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Another example is the Genius Society: There is no shortage of eccentrics like Madam Herta who dedicate themselves to scientific research under the protection of the Erudition.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: These factions possess the same power as us to voyage between worlds. It would be hard to travel through the galaxy without them.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The birth of an Aeon gives rise to a Path. The nature of the Paths remains a mystery, leaving us to draw an analogy in a way that mortals can understand: It's a philosophical concept of sorts.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: A person is considered to be on a Path when their will overlaps with that Path. If the person has a strong enough will, they can draw power from that Path. Those who can do so are called Pathstriders.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Pathstriders possess extraordinary power, but are still insignificant compared to the Aeons, like a drop of water in a vast ocean. Sometimes, Aeons will bestow a mortal with their power, making them an "Emanator" of that Aeon.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I should mention that once a Path is open, it cannot be closed, even with the fall of its Aeon. That is how we are still able to travel across the stars, despite Akivili's passing.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: "What you saw was the simulated Aeon carefully cultivated by Ruan Mei and Screwllum. The simulated Aeons will ignore us just like the real ones, so I set your simulated identity as Akivili, Aeon of Trailblaze, to attract THEM." With a click of her tongue, Herta says, "Now it seems that my judgment is correct. Next time you run into the Aeons, try to get something out of THEM."
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: About Exploration...
About Understanding...
About Establishing...
About Connection...
I have another question...
Explore the unknown world to continue our journey ahead.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Understand the local culture and immerse ourselves within it.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Establish a connection with the new world — rejoice with it and share in its fears.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Connect worlds together, carving an endless path.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: What do you want to know?
You must know more about gossip than I do!
About our companions...
About Stellarons...
About the Antimatter Legion...
About the Fragmentum...
I don't have any other questions.
"Myths of the Aeons, anecdotes, love stories, the origin of the universe... Anything will do!" Herta was annoyed, "Just think of something!"
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: About Himeko...
About Pom-Pom...
About Dan Heng...
About March 7th...
I have another question...
Haha, she's the owner of the Express. We joke around calling Pom-Pom the conductor, but everyone knows Himeko is the boss.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: It all started with her encounter with the Astral Express, and they haven't been apart since then.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: She's... extremely passionate, like a burning sun. However, she remains mysterious most of the time. Once in a while, you feel that she's burning herself out trying to accomplish her dream.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Only someone like her is worthy of the Astral Express. I think Himeko's vision of her whole life revolves around... a very important dream.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: To be honest, I don't know when Pom-Pom appeared... I think it was before I came to the Express? No wait, maybe it was after...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Pom-Pom is like the spirit of the Astral Express. Whenever anyone on the Express needs help, they will appear immediately. It would be ill-advised to underestimate them.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Pom-Pom is terrifying when they get angry... Yes, terrifying...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Dan Heng is a lonely child. He may appear distant and cold, but his heart is kind. Perhaps, he's the way he is today because he spent so much time on the run. Sometimes, he reminds me of myself when I was young...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: We don't know what he's running from. He once told me that he didn't know either. All he knew was that something was chasing him and that he had to run away — first from the Xianzhou, then the IPC.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: So he boarded the ship of a troupe called the "Mourning Actors" and escaped the IPC. After a while he made his way to the Express, and he's stayed here longer than anywhere else.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Don't worry, no matter who or what wants to hurt Dan Heng, we won't let them. Those who dare attack members of the Astral Express should be prepared to suffer the wrath of me and Himeko.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Did Himeko tell you about March 7th? She was trapped in ice, floating through space. We happened upon her and rescued her.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: It was a unique type of ice known as Six-Phased Ice — a substance that adheres to Imaginary Law, meaning that external forces cannot change its form.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Whoever sealed her inside the Six-Phased Ice... No matter who it is... did so either to protect or banish her. I believe she had been floating through space for some time.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Be sure to collect Preservation Blessings, okay? See if we can get Qlipoth to visit once more.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Bring it on...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Darn it...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Well, THEY probably won't come.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Sorry, I temporarily revoked your activity permissions — Uh, I need to apologize to you about something.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: I confess, I'm a little too eager for success... I won't interfere with the system again. Just play as you like.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Qlipoth's appearance was probably just a coincidence... That's it. Anyway, I'm sorry.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: The fight is over and you wait in place, but nothing happens.
rows.speaker: Simulated Universe

rows.text: There is a long silence, followed by a deep sigh from Herta. "I was expecting THEM to appear. Never mind. I'll switch off the Simulated Universe then. It'll only take a second and you won't feel a thing. Let's chat back in reality."
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: "THEY... came!" You hear Herta's stunned words. "No, not THEM... It's another Aeon! It's..." Her voice suddenly drifts off. You have a strange feeling about this, as if Herta's words solidified and the whole Simulated Universe became somehow unreal.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: You see a blurry figure made of mirror fragments, and THEIR facial features are repeatedly refracted by the prism to form a mystery. Countless memories spring up before your eyes.
rows.speaker: Fuli

rows.text: You see Kafka. Her body is stretched, deformed, and rubbed together with the umbrella in her hand, turning into water droplets and falling at your feet.
rows.speaker: Fuli

rows.text: You find yourself become a weeping Adlivun baby with an uncut umbilical cord. You remember that there is a golden scar on your body, and golden blood flowing on the dying planet. You find yourself dark-skinned and wearing a robe on the wasteland. You find that you are a swift shadow across the abyss, reaching out to catch the shooting star.
rows.speaker: Fuli

rows.text: The Interastral Peace Corporation's after-sales service is very comprehensive. The vending machine has a wide range of products that are regularly refreshed.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Hyper-distant delivery costs an arm and a leg, but we got this machine from Madam Herta, all the products inside come free of shipping charges.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Then, THEIR voice suddenly came... "...robe flutter wrap travel you expand dark skin you laugh explore thread rotation intertwine coordinate weave ocean vocabulary..." Every word THEY say is connected to each other like a whisper. Before you could say anything, THEY suddenly disappear.
rows.speaker: Fuli

rows.text: Wait, let's talk about Kafka.
THEY have controlled my brain!
You said you wouldn't interfere anymore —
Success! I have to tell this news to Stephen right away — [Trailblazer], don't just stand there. Go in and see if you can get a few more words out of them or something...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: You should show me some respect.
You have no right to order me around.
Alright, I'll go now then.
Oh, you're right. I got too excited... Sorry, [Trailblazer]. I do respect you! If you don't mind, could you please go in for another test?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Oh, you're right. I got too excited... Sorry, [Trailblazer]. You did very well! If you don't mind, could you please go in for another test?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: I've upgraded the Simulated Universe — it now has more memory and can support longer sessions. The last round must've been pretty boring — I'll get Stephen to add a few more interesting things.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: This part was made specifically with you in mind. Ready to have some fun?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Yay! I love fun games!
Not as good as adding more rewards...
I don't trust the definition of "interesting" around here...
Stephen said the same thing. I don't really get "fun," but whatever. What's more important is that the rewards will also increase!
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Oh, but we will — after all, you're gonna be spending more time on this project.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: What can I say? I don't trust it either. For some reason, whenever someone tells me they're gonna do something interesting, I end up imagining a pile of trash...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: ...so I'd rather talk with you about the added rewards part.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: I'll help you out some more. Don't worry.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Can I still return to the space station?
Whether they are enemies from the abyss or people with ill intentions...
rows.speaker: Capote

rows.text: Great. Looks like your stamina is really quite special.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: This is a shy, full-length mirror. No matter how much you fiddle with it, it won't move.
This mirror doesn't reflect your appearance. Maybe it only wants to show March 7th's.
This is a full-length mirror with frosted glass. It may have some kind of hidden meaning.
You don't quite understand why exactly March 7th has bought this mirror.
The photos on this wall flash and blink, filled with memories of your adventures.
After staring at it for a while, you realize that the memories on this wall aren't just "your" adventures.
This is kinda creepy, man. How did you manage to shoot some of these angles?
You're pretty sure some of the pictures on this wall have been captured without a camera.
Not even March 7th is there.
What a mysterious photo wall.
This cozy rest area is in stark contrast to Dan Heng's sparse floor bed next door.
This velvet blanket is soft to the touch and feels comfortable. Sitting on it feels just as comfortable; not sure about sleeping on it, though.
There's a bunny-shaped lounge chair with a teddy bear sitting in it. A fitting metaphor for their conflicted owner.
A doll in the form of Conductor Pom-Pom. It doesn't have any clothes.
A doll in the form of Conductor Pom-Pom. Its colors are a bit faded.
A doll in the form of Conductor Pom-Pom. Looking at it makes you feel embarrassed.
A doll in the form of Conductor Pom-Pom. You have no idea where they've found it.
A doll in the form of Conductor Pom-Pom. So that's what they look like without clothes.
March 7th's bed. It's not very tidy.
March 7th's bed. There's a rabbit pillow and a bear pillow.
March 7th's bed. Several photos are casually strewn on the duvet.
March 7th's bed. Half of it is neatly made, and the other half, not.
March 7th's bed. Intuition tells you that should be comfier than Dan Heng's.
March 7th's desk. All kinds of gizmos are strewn about it.
The computer station on the table comes pre-installed with the IPC's "Eidor" operating system. It's a genuine copy.
The computer station on the table comes preinstalled with the IPC's "Eidor" operating system. This OS might just cost more than the whole computer system.
March 7th's desk looks neater than her bed does.
March 7th's desk. You fail to see anything that resembles a diary.
So this little twerp has the Stellaron now? Huh.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: When I first woke up after being rescued from the ice, I could see clusters of stars in front of me. I reached out for them automatically, but they turned out to be the carriage ceiling lights.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The whole crew was watching me — it was pretty embarrassing...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Oh, I forgot to tell you.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Before all this, I was stuck in a huge block of ice drifting through space.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Uh-huh! Like I was some kind of weird alien! I don't really blame them for being curious though — they had no idea where I came from.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You might not believe it, but before all this, I was stuck in a huge block of ice drifting through space.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Himeko and Mr. Yang and... who was it again? Anyway, they figured out a way to melt the ice and saved me.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Who knows? I don't remember anything before that.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I don't remember a thing.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Who I am, where I'm from, my name... it's like everything was erased from my mind. "March 7th" was the day they found me, so it stuck.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Ever since then, I've been hanging out on this train and following it to whatever destination it decides to stop at. I'm hoping that one day, I can find my past...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Ugh, what am I talking about this for? Way to get everyone down, huh.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It's fine. I was the one who brought it up.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Cheer up, [Trailblazer]! It's not every day someone gets to ride on the Astral Express...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Ah, here comes the conductor!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The Express has reached a safe distance from the space station. We'll be jumping in about ten minutes.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Return to your seats please, both of you. Things could get bumpy!
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Uh... thanks, Pom-Pom. But did you really have to come and remind me? I'm not a newbie, you know~
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The door is shut tight...
Well, it wouldn't be necessary, but Miss March 7th likes to challenge herself... and falls over every time.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: That's just called never giving up! Hehe~
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Oh, don't worry about me. I just wanna see if I can stay on my feet this time~
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Good luck, I'm rooting for you.
Don't hurt yourself.
Why do you make things hard for yourself?
Thanks. I feel like I'm starting to get the hang of it.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The key is using your core, waist, and leg muscles. It's not your stance that matters, but your ability to ride the inertia...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It's fine, I'm sturdier than I look~ Besides, the ice will protect me.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: When I'm in danger, I instinctively create ice to protect myself.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Though sometimes falling on the ice actually hurts more than falling on the ground.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Don't be silly — this is fun!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I like keeping busy, otherwise I start obsessing over... pointless things.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Well, don't mind me. Find a place to sit down and buckle up.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Our next stop is a small planet called Jarilo-VI.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: It's been thousands of years since the last time the Express paid a visit. The data bank shows it was a lush and beautiful place.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: But after all this time, it's possible that dramatic changes have occurred.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Jumps are like this: They may feel novel the first few times, but you'll slowly get used to them after a few more.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: As for the mechanism... Well, if you're interested, I'll explain it to you in detail when we have more time.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: For now, just sit and wait. Remember to close your eyes — it helps with the dizziness.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: (Hmm... Maybe Dan Heng locked it?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]
